resources.string: Simplified teaching animation. The paths, amounts, and timing are illustrative, not measurements.
The tongue moves the bolus back
Chewing and saliva help form a soft bolus. The tongue sends it toward the throat, and the airway is briefly protected as the bolus enters the esophagus.
A wave of contraction moves food
Muscle contracts behind the food and relaxes ahead of it. This wave pushes the bolus toward the stomach; the lower sphincter relaxes to let it pass.
Stomach muscle mixes food and digestive juice
The stomach churns food with acid and digestive enzymes. Enzymes begin breaking down proteins, and small portions of chyme pass through the pylorus.
Bile and pancreatic juice join the chyme
Bile disperses fat into small droplets. Pancreatic enzymes help digest fats, carbohydrates and proteins; intestinal enzymes continue the process.
Simple sugars and amino acids enter blood capillaries. Most absorbed long-chain fats are repackaged in intestinal cells and enter the lymphatic vessel.
How the large intestine recovers water
After the small intestine has absorbed most nutrients, the remaining liquid and undigested material pass from the ileum into the cecum.
Short segments of the colon squeeze at different times. This mixes the contents and brings them into contact with the colon lining.
The colon absorbs some of the remaining water and salts. As water moves out of the contents, the material becomes more solid.
Occasional stronger waves move material farther along the colon toward the rectum. This movement differs from local mixing.
The rectum stores stool before release
The rectum holds stool. During a bowel movement, rectal contraction and relaxation of the outlet muscles allow it to leave.
